description: [NAM] There is a long-running myth that Africans did not have clothes until the arrival of Arabs and later, colonisation. In fact, Africa has a long tradition of making its own unique clothing since time immemorial. From Malian mud cloths, which they say are made of the earth, the river and the sun, to the famous red Maasai Shuka, clothes across the continent carry with them deep and complex histories both local and global. Jamila Versi takes a deeper look at the story behind Ugandan bark cloth and speaks to
title: Africa: The Cloth Made From the Tree of Life

description: [allAfrica] At dawn in Enugu State, a crate of tomatoes begins a race against the heat. For the woman who grew them, the harvest should mean income: school fees, wages and seed for the next planting season. But without reliable cold storage, she faces a difficult choice. Sell quickly, often at the price offered, or wait and risk watching her harvest spoil.
title: Africa: How Reliable Energy Can Turn a Woman's Harvest Into a Thriving Business
